Welcome to St Mary's Catholic Primary School
Welcome to our wonderful school! I am extremely proud to be the Headteacher of St Mary’s Catholic Primary School and I am passionate about everyone doing their very best for this much-loved school. The fundamental aim of our school, and the very reason for our existence, is to enable each child who attends to be all that they can be - to embrace and fulfil their unique, God-given potential.We are very proud of the Catholic faith foundation of our school and work very hard to ensure the Gospel Values, that permeate both our daily life and the curriculum we deliver, are reflected in our environment and how we relate to one another. We are an inclusive school and welcome pupils from all backgrounds, there are no barriers to our welcome.

St Mary's Catholic Primary School - National Year of Reading 2026
pageCache.text:
Our School
National Year of Reading 2026
Families across the country are being invited to join a nationwide celebration of books as England launches its National Year of Reading 2026. The campaign, led by the Department for Education and the National Literacy Trust, aims to spark a love of reading in children and adults alike. Reading for pleasure has been declining in recent years, with fewer children saying they enjoy reading in their free time. This matters because regular reading is linked to stronger learning, better wellbeing, and greater confidence. The Year of Reading hopes to turn this around with the message: “If you’re into it, read into it.” Whether a child loves football, animals, art, or outer space, there’s a book that can bring that passion to life. Throughout 2026, schools, libraries, and community groups will be hosting events, challenges, and activities to help families discover the joy of reading together. Even ten minutes a day can make a huge difference; sharing a story, exploring a comic, or reading about something your child already loves. Reading with your child isn’t just educational; it’s a moment of connection, curiosity, and imagination. This year is the perfect time to build a reading habit that lasts long after 2026 ends.
Keep a look out for our resources and updates that will be posted here over the year.

Our School
Safeguarding and Pastoral Care
At St Mary’s Catholic Primary School, we see the wellbeing of our children and staff as a priority. Our Pastoral Care Worker is available for children and parents to talk to about any worries or concerns they may have. We then help children, and their families access the support they need whether that’s through 1 to 1 or small group work in school looking at emotions, building self-esteem and helping self-expression, or through accessing external support.
External support services include parenting classes, Family Outreach Workers, health services, Play Therapy, Counselling and Young Carer’s services. We have seen these really benefit our pupils and their famillies.
We hope that through identifying each child and family’s needs and offering the support that’s required, we can help make each pupils journey through primary school as successful as possible.
‘Everyone within our community is encouraged to strive for the highest standards of personal, social and intellectual development.
